r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/<work-id>/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from <work-id> alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

r4g.title: Criterion 7: judge the six choices (outermost-two freeze)
r4g.imperative: Render independent judgment on whether freezing only the outermost two gates per spine is right, given the human's 'frozen at start/finish, squishy middle' framing and Commander's review/feedback deliberately left mutable.
r4g.finding: Freezing exactly outermost-two per spine is the right cut, but I traced the downstream-enforcement gap the handoff's rationale glosses over. Verified: Commander archive's postconditions (c1-c4) never reference review's user-decision evidence, so dropping review removes human sign-off with NO downstream enforcement. feedback is different: archive c1 mechanically requires an episode to exist for this work_id (verify_episode_captured.py scans the store), so dropping the feedback GATE doesn't bypass that invariant -- it's enforced by state, not by gate completion. Explorer shows the same asymmetry: route's precondition p1 ('spec confirmed') and postcondition c1 are both check:null (self-attested), so dropping confirm (the ONE gate with a mechanical user-decision artifact check) removes the only machine-enforced human sign-off with nothing pulling it back at route. Admiral avoids this: closeout's own c5 bakes 'epic summary accepted by human' (artifact/user-decision) directly onto the FROZEN bookend, so it cannot be dropped away regardless of what happens to the mutable middle. Judgment: the six declarations are correct as scoped and I would not block on this, but Admiral's pattern (bake the human-decision postcondition onto the frozen closing gate itself) is strictly more robust than Commander's/Explorer's (leave the decision on a droppable middle gate and hope archive/route's other checks compensate) -- for feedback the compensation happens to hold (episode-existence is state-checked), for review/confirm it does not. Flagging as a triage candidate, not a blocker on this diff.

Fowler pass: all 12 baseline smells absent. Two required test suites reproduced green matching implementer's tallies exactly.

triage_candidates.statement: Commander's archive and Explorer's route do not mechanically verify that the human-confirmation step (review's user-decision / confirm's user-decision) actually happened before the closing bookend completes -- dropping the middle review/confirm gate removes the only machine-enforced sign-off with nothing downstream re-enforcing it. Admiral's closeout already bakes its human-decision postcondition (c5) directly onto the frozen bookend; consider the same pattern for Commander archive and Explorer route so the mutable middle can't quietly drop the human-confirmation requirement. Not a blocker on #634/g2 -- the six declarations it shipped are correct as scoped -- but worth a follow-up issue.
